key_idea: Assuming finitely many minimal hypersurfaces, attaching cylindrical ends to a stable core yields a sequence of min-max widths whose asymptotic linear growth arithmetically contradicts the areas of the trapped hypersurfaces via Weyl's equidistribution theorem.
reason: The proof achieves a monumental result with an extraordinarily clean and surprising structure. It brilliantly bridges geometric measure theory and number theory, using Diophantine approximation to extract a forced geometric contradiction from the volume spectrum.
recognized: Antoine Song, Existence of infinitely many minimal hypersurfaces in closed manifolds (Yau's conjecture)
